title: The Horde adaptive soundtrack composition brief
status: Proposed music direction grounded in approved campaign planning; not a runtime implementation or mastered audio claim

motif_contract.identity: Preserve the chromatic D–Eb–A–E–D opening. Nominal D minor is not permission to quantize the melody to that scale. Original major-colour G/H payoff already exists: new hopeful ending may draw on its F# rather than claim a newly invented major resolution.
motif_contract.drone: The A/D held third-part removal is already applied. Keep the short A4 opening note; do not reintroduce the held material or label this a pending fix.
motif_contract.new_material: K and H in the original prose meant proposed companion/home answers, not Chordsmith section letters. Rename proposed secondary themes COMPANION and HOME to avoid collision with A–H engine section names.

sound_world: Historical-gothic dark fantasy with small acoustic-seeming ensembles, deliberate silence, dread, wonder and homecoming. No borrowed Zelda melodies, Perfect Dark pastiche, modern drum-kit groove, synth arpeggiator or sci-fi sound design. Engine synthesis may approximate instruments but must be described honestly.

cues.title: What the Dark Keeps
cues.motif_transformation: The verified original theme is the source; preserve its recognizable melodic interval/rhythm cell M and avoid claiming new notes are canonical.
cues.target_palette: Low bowed strings, plucked lute/harp, breathy flute, sparse bell and warm organ-like sustain.
cues.section_plan: 8-bar invitation; 32-bar quiet A; 32-bar fuller B; 4-bar turnaround; 4-bar new-game exit. These are larger musical forms assembled from supported 1–4-bar blocks, not unsupported 16–32-bar section objects.
cues.dynamic_states_and_canon: Quiet title; focused menu; optional fuller title statement. No spoilers in track metadata.

cues.title: The Fourth Keeper's Rest
cues.location_purpose: Northwest abandoned Keeper Tomb, opening corridors and waterfall guards
cues.motif_transformation: M is incomplete and low, with wide rests and unresolved final note; it describes custody and the buried past.
cues.target_palette: Bowed low strings, dry low drum, restrained high harmonics and stone-like resonances.
cues.section_plan: 4-bar entry; two contrasting 16-bar exploration loops; 16-bar guard-threat loop; 2-bar threat bridge; 4-bar retreat/recovery. These are larger musical forms assembled from supported 1–4-bar blocks, not unsupported 16–32-bar section objects.
cues.dynamic_states_and_canon: Stillness; exploration; guards alerted/combat; safe aftermath. Kit's early grate call ducks the music. No lantern-associated reveal before reward.

cues.title: The Jailer's Last Vigil
cues.location_purpose: Prologue cursed fourth keeper boss and lantern reward
cues.motif_transformation: M becomes a stern defensive phrase rather than an evil-theme caricature; the defeat reduces to a questioning fragment.
cues.target_palette: Bowed strings, bass drone, restrained horn-like tone, hand drums and sparse dissonant bell.
cues.section_plan: 4-bar reveal; 16-bar guarded loop; 16-bar pressured loop; 2-bar transition; 4-bar defeat; 8-bar quiet reward. These are larger musical forms assembled from supported 1–4-bar blocks, not unsupported 16–32-bar section objects.
cues.dynamic_states_and_canon: Proposed music states: reveal, active defence, late pressure, confirmed defeat, lantern claim. Phase entry follows gameplay events, not a fixed recording timeline; attack tells remain independent.

cues.title: Beneath the Same Moon
cues.location_purpose: Rope rescue, Kit reunion, moonlit forest, lookout chapter endpoint
cues.motif_transformation: M receives a softer answering phrase COMPANION, a new proposal representing companionship rather than a voiced player response.
cues.target_palette: Recorder/flute-like lead, small plucked strings, warm bowed strings, very sparse frame drum.
cues.section_plan: 4-bar ascent bridge; 16-bar reunion; two 16-bar trail loops; 8-bar uncanny waystone insert; 8-bar lookout arrival; 4-bar reversible return. These are larger musical forms assembled from supported 1–4-bar blocks, not unsupported 16–32-bar section objects.
cues.dynamic_states_and_canon: Relief; quiet travel; optional threat overlay; lantern clue; lookout vista. Remain nocturnal, never announce dawn or curse lifted. Kit dialogue gets long rests.

cues.title: The Roads of Veyr
cues.location_purpose: Shared regional paths, outbound junction, minor shrine, approach links
cues.motif_transformation: M becomes a walking figure; destination timbres enter before the next area. Starter shrine stretches it into a contemplative phrase.
cues.target_palette: Plucked lute/harp, soft fiddle/strings and hand drum; regional bell, metallic or glass accents as variants.
cues.section_plan: 4-bar entry; 32-bar road loop; 16-bar shrine loop; 8-bar south/east/ridge approach variants; 2/4-bar destination bridges; 4-bar retreat exit. These are larger musical forms assembled from supported 1–4-bar blocks, not unsupported 16–32-bar section objects.
cues.dynamic_states_and_canon: Travel; hesitation/access task; threat; safe shrine; completed return. No separate songs for each upgrade route. Use destination overlays only when narratively appropriate.

cues.title: Bellwether, Still Burning
cues.location_purpose: Unwalled village hub, tavern/well, services, churchyard, mill
cues.motif_transformation: M is answered with COMPANION in a modest communal tune HOME; warmth and belonging temper greed without pretending danger is over.
cues.target_palette: Lute/harp, fiddle-like strings, woodwind, soft frame drum; occasional church-bell timbre treated separately from actual bell SFX.
cues.section_plan: 4-bar arrival; 32-bar hub loop; 16-bar hearth variant; 16-bar churchyard/records variant; 16-bar restrained concerned-return variant; 4-bar departure. These are larger musical forms assembled from supported 1–4-bar blocks, not unsupported 16–32-bar section objects.
cues.dynamic_states_and_canon: Streets; tavern/services; reflective churchyard; story-changed return. Mill/smith activity stays diegetic SFX; don't commission full tracks per shop or infer a supernatural bell event.
cues.feel: Original musical proposal is6/8. Immediate4/4 lilt is a verified-schema staging option; evaluate true compound meter rather than permanently constrain the score.

cues.title: Bells Beneath the Water
cues.location_purpose: Southern lake vista, submerged access, mostly dry Abbey interiors and light puzzles
cues.motif_transformation: M is spaced like a broken liturgy; answering fragments suggest reflected light, without audio alone revealing the puzzle solution.
cues.target_palette: Low bowed strings, restrained organ-like sustain, bell partials, plucked high notes, breathy wind.
cues.section_plan: 8-bar lake vista; 8-bar crossing loop; 16-bar dry arrival; two 16-bar interior loops; 16-bar tension loop; 2-bar bridges; 4-bar post-seal return. These are larger musical forms assembled from supported 1–4-bar blocks, not unsupported 16–32-bar section objects.
cues.dynamic_states_and_canon: Vista; short crossing; dry exploration; reflector practice/puzzle; duty-hall threat; post-seal reflection. Muffled texture belongs only to crossing/wet views, not the whole dry dungeon. No ocean palette.

cues.title: The Bellkeeper
cues.motif_transformation: M is a measured bell/processional figure, opened into a clear higher-register answer during valid reflected-light exposure.
cues.target_palette: Low strings, bell accents, restrained organ, frame/bass drum and sparse higher plucked line.
cues.section_plan: 4-bar entrance; 16-bar armoured loop; 8/16-bar exposure variant; 16-bar final-pressure loop; 2-bar reset bridge; 4-bar defeat; 8-bar seal/relic release. These are larger musical forms assembled from supported 1–4-bar blocks, not unsupported 16–32-bar section objects.
cues.dynamic_states_and_canon: Armoured; reflected-light setup; actual exposure; recovery; final pressure if gameplay supports it; confirmed defeat. Music supports the learned reflector/shutter rule; never creates a mandatory rhythm puzzle or masks warnings.

cues.title: The King's Account
cues.location_purpose: Eastern gorge approach, royal mint/forge, labour and stand puzzles
cues.motif_transformation: M is reduced to repeated work-shaped cells with displaced accents; a held tone mirrors leaving light in place while moving.
cues.target_palette: Dry hammered-string/plucked metal approximations, bowed low strings, muted hand drums and sparse bell; no modern industrial beat.
cues.section_plan: 8-bar gorge vista; 16-bar access loop; two 16-bar mint/work loops; 16-bar tension loop; 8-bar stand-practice sparse variant; 2/4-bar bridges; 4-bar return. These are larger musical forms assembled from supported 1–4-bar blocks, not unsupported 16–32-bar section objects.
cues.dynamic_states_and_canon: Approach; machinery exploration; stand lesson; smoke/cover pressure; cleared archive. Harmonic treatment cannot imply Abbey already happened. Mechanical hazards/timing have independent audible cues.

cues.title: Master of Coin
cues.motif_transformation: M is compressed and insistently repeated; the answer opens only for earned mechanism/exposure windows.
cues.target_palette: Low strings, plucked metal-like pulse, hand/bass drums, restrained brass-like layer; limited bright transients.
cues.section_plan: 4-bar entrance; 16-bar enclosed-shell loop; 16-bar hold-light/reposition loop; 8-bar exposure variant; 16-bar escalation; 2-bar reset; 4-bar defeat; 8-bar seal/archive. These are larger musical forms assembled from supported 1–4-bar blocks, not unsupported 16–32-bar section objects.
cues.dynamic_states_and_canon: Shell protected; mechanism maintained; exposed; recovery; later pressure if authored; confirmed defeat. Keep soundscape gaps for fire, shutter and attack tells. No industrial/electronic or science-fiction identity.

cues.title: A Garden Behind Glass
cues.location_purpose: Northeastern ridge, ruined mirrored palace and roofless winter garden
cues.motif_transformation: M becomes elegant and clearer in counterpoint; incomplete imitations suggest preserved beauty and contradictory history.
cues.target_palette: Harp/plucked strings, high bowed strings, celesta-like glass approximations, soft woodwind and restrained organ.
cues.section_plan: 8-bar ridge reveal; two 16-bar garden/palace loops; 16-bar aperture/records sparse loop; 16-bar tension; 2/4-bar bridges; 4-bar return. These are larger musical forms assembled from supported 1–4-bar blocks, not unsupported 16–32-bar section objects.
cues.dynamic_states_and_canon: Ridge/gate; winter garden; mirrored gallery; aperture lesson; royal records; approaching keeper. Both seals gate access; musical evolution may reflect that completed history. Reflections are finite, not a demand for spatial audio gimmicks.

cues.title: The Last Lucid Keeper
cues.location_purpose: Glass Court keeper encounter and prison revelation
cues.motif_transformation: M and its previously hidden answering contour trade registers; protection sounds sorrowful and purposeful. Do not use a triumphant kill cadence.
cues.target_palette: Bowed strings in measured imitation, plucked glass/harp, restrained low drums and organ-like sustain.
cues.section_plan: 4-bar recognition; 16-bar warded loop; 16-bar receiver-selection loop; 8-bar protection-broken variant; 2-bar regroup; 4-bar defeat-without-death exit; 8-bar revelation bed. These are larger musical forms assembled from supported 1–4-bar blocks, not unsupported 16–32-bar section objects.
cues.dynamic_states_and_canon: Recognition/dialogue; wards intact; learned aperture action; vulnerability; confirmed defeat; evidence/revelation. Exact boss staging/survival remains undecided; state names must not hard-code killing.

cues.title: All That Was Carried Home
cues.location_purpose: Dry vault beneath/behind Court ridge, real riches, ritual and release
cues.motif_transformation: M returns with genuine beauty; Abbey, Foundry and Court colours become recognizable echoes of plundered objects. Suspicion grows through harmonic context, not an early villain reveal.
cues.target_palette: Harp/lute, broad strings, restrained bell/metal/glass colours; warm organ-like underpinning.
cues.section_plan: 8-bar first vista; 32-bar treasure loop; 16-bar ritual preparation; 8-bar held ritual transition; 4-bar release bridge with interrupt-safe cut. These are larger musical forms assembled from supported 1–4-bar blocks, not unsupported 16–32-bar section objects.
cues.dynamic_states_and_canon: Awe; examine riches; prepare ritual; genuine release of soldiers; entity freed. Sequence triggered by authored events; players may linger indefinitely. This is compact finale staging, not a fourth full dungeon.

cues.title: What the Dark Releases
cues.motif_transformation: M appears in its most forceful distorted rhythm/register against the human COMPANION/HOME answer. Its recognizable identity is retained rather than replaced by generic boss music.
cues.target_palette: Bowed strings, low organ/drone, hand/bass drums, horn-like reinforcement and carefully rationed bell; no electronic drop.
cues.section_plan: 4-bar rupture; 16-bar confrontation A; 16-bar escalation B; 16-bar culmination C; 2/4-bar bridges; 4-bar confirmed defeat; 8-bar release. These are larger musical forms assembled from supported 1–4-bar blocks, not unsupported 16–32-bar section objects.
cues.dynamic_states_and_canon: Proposed musical phases only: confrontation, escalating pressure, culmination, actual defeat. No invented entity form, name, attack or new mandatory power. A/B/C can be selected by future authored encounter events.

cues.title: Enough to Come Home
cues.location_purpose: Playable return to Bellwether, hopeful epilogue and credits
cues.motif_transformation: M finally receives a settled answer from COMPANION/HOME; the ending is earned, modest and hopeful, not proof of a specific treasure distribution or daylight.
cues.target_palette: Warm small strings, recorder/flute, lute/harp, light frame drum and sparse bell.
cues.section_plan: 8-bar release/road entry; 32-bar playable-return loop; 16-bar village reprise; 32-bar credits expansion; 8-bar final cadence. These are larger musical forms assembled from supported 1–4-bar blocks, not unsupported 16–32-bar section objects.
cues.dynamic_states_and_canon: Return road; changed home; quiet epilogue; optional credits. One ending only; no alternate keeper branch. Keep full unresolved narrative decisions out of music labels.
cues.feel: Original musical proposal is6/8. Immediate4/4 lilt is a verified-schema staging option; evaluate true compound meter rather than permanently constrain the score.

common_composition_contract.forms: Compose short A–H blocks and sequences within actual schema17 caps. Supply explicit proposed state-to-section/sequence metadata. Loops must be able to extend for gameplay, but runtime switching is not implied by a rendered listening assembly.
common_composition_contract.lengths: Each actual section 1–4 bars. Larger 16/32-bar musical forms are assembled using at most64 sequence slots. One-shots can use the suitable short section, trimmed only through an exact documented render/export process.
common_composition_contract.stems: Do not promise independent runtime stems. If actual renderer supports isolated parts, label them verified offline stems; otherwise deliver explicit section arrangements. Layer/state intentions remain proposal metadata.
common_composition_contract.runtime_boundary: Composer deliverable includes sections and transition intent. In-game state dispatch, streaming, ducking, resume and safety are a future integration contract, not claimed implemented.
common_composition_contract.tonality: Preserve motif intervals/rhythm or a documented deliberate transformation. Reharmonization should keep M recognizable without quoting the complete theme in every room. Use minor/modal ambiguity, open fifths and restrained dissonance; major-coloured homecoming need not overwrite the original motif.
common_composition_contract.branch_order: Abbey and Foundry share neither mandatory melodic dependence nor first/second story assumptions. Use seal_count/revelation flags only for small optional narrative inserts, not duplicate entire scores.

stingers.purpose: Optional secret discovery; modest M fragment, cooldown and deduplication.
Local tool acquired; same family with reflector/stand/aperture timbre variants.
Confirmed light interaction; unobtrusive acknowledgment, no premature solution hint.
Confirmed route/gate opens; one variant of light-solved family where useful.
Persistent seal award; peer versions equivalent, final Court variant fuller.
Rare uncanny clue/revelation insert, only after lantern owned; never automatically over every line.
Player death/failure; end combat, do not replay reward or spoiler material.
Optional restrained retry pickup; often silence is better.
Confirmed boss defeat, variant appropriate to area; Court version does not imply death.

implementation_constraints: Pause must preserve musical transport/state or enter a short held release safely; do not start title music over paused exploration. Resume must not layer duplicate voices or stale combat loops.
Music, dialogue and SFX use separate controls. Duck music around Kit, NPC, entity and keeper speech; priority attack/exposure warning SFX remain intelligible with music muted and in mono.

Do not compose a normal rope-loading-screen cue: ascent and descent have no normal loading screen by approved contract. Carry a compatible bed across the hidden transition; reserve a quiet neutral holding bed for genuine recovery/failure only.
Variable-length loads cannot depend on a composed crescendo completing. Retain a non-spoiler hold and safe fade; don't imply all regions require loading screens.

Use debounced/hysteretic danger states and musical transition boundaries for area changes. Urgent combat/death SFX cannot wait for bar boundaries. Cancel queued obsolete states and reward stingers after death/reload.
Independent state must restore area, completed seal/reward flags, encounter status and motif reveal permissions. Never replay one-time narrative reveals on ordinary backtracking.

Validate loop sample boundaries, audio tails, phase continuity, crossfades, rapid event changes, pause/background/resume, interrupted boss/retry, mono/headphones/phone speaker, all sliders and both middle-dungeon orders.

Target sample format, loudness, true-peak, voice count, storage, codec and stream-memory budgets require actual engine audit and device evidence. Suggested mastering target should be labelled provisional, not a passed spec.

No paid tools or purchased samples. Original authored note scores and engine synthesis only unless a separately verified source is approved. Record composer/source provenance, motif source, synthesis-engine revision and any sample licenses. Do not assert exclusivity or legal copyright certainty for generated material.
next_steps: Replace symbolic motif M with verified source-note/rhythm reference and inspect exact engine schema.
Convert all 15 families into valid Pocket Chordsmith scores using supported sections/instruments; retain proposed-state maps separately if runtime switching is absent.
Render short first-pass listening assemblies plus every gameplay loop/bridge/exit; identify synthesized previews versus mastered final assets.
Validate notes, durations, clipped peaks, silence, loop joins and motif recurrence; listen to each distinct family and representative transitions.
Package score sources, per-section audio, human tracklist, cue manifest and validation evidence. Runtime registration, code changes, repository writes and public release are out of this assignment.

actual_engine_contract.migration: Original source schema16 must use canonicalizePcsProject(raw).project and current validator.
actual_engine_contract.project_strategy: 15 separate project banks; each has at most A–H. Stingers in one or more separate banks only when needed. Never make 15 sections in one project.
actual_engine_contract.section_bars: 1–4 bars each; use max4 for each distinct block, sequence repeats/contrasts to form longer listening loops. A state needing more than one block gets a bounded sequence, not an oversized section.
actual_engine_contract.state_map_warning: A–H assignments are bank-specific. The map is composition metadata only until an integration consumer actually implements and tests it.
adaptive_caveats: Browser Core has beat/bar quantization; its section quantization currently means bar, not section-end.
Stingers currently emit events; an event alone does not play a rendered sound.
thenReturnTo is stored without execution; do not rely on automatic return.
Proposed stems, streaming, dialogue ducking, state persistence and cross-region handoff are not verified by this composition task.
actual_engine_contract.existing_game_contract: Keep current native eight-cue integration untouched. Native loop cues are 12 seconds, C is 3 seconds, G is 6 seconds, tails 3 seconds and crossfades 250 ms. New soundtrack is a future integration package, not a replacement manifest accepted by the game.
actual_engine_contract.instrument_mapping: Existing source lead cowboy_whistle, second soft_pluck, third mellow_sax. New acoustic-seeming palettes are target timbres only. Composer must map them to actual engine-supported voice IDs; label approximation and do not claim sampled live instruments.

engine_evolution.principle: The music can drive engine evolution. Current restrictions bound what is verified today, not the artistic design. Current-schema previews are staging assets, not a requirement to reduce the eventual soundtrack to eight cues.

requirements.need: Explicit time signature, tempo, phrase length and section-end boundaries; true 6/8 town/homecoming if selected musically.
requirements.acceptance: Tests distinguish beat, bar, phrase and section boundaries, including meter/tempo changes; deterministic sample scheduling remains coherent across long playback and pause/resume.

requirements.feature: Independent section forms and project scale
requirements.need: Variable-length entries, loops, bridges and exits; named sections and projects beyond fixed A–H where needed.
requirements.acceptance: Round-trip authored forms without truncation; migration preserves existing source scores and current eight-cue game compatibility; validate IDs, lengths and transition graph.

requirements.need: Trigger actual audio and resume/return to a specified state safely, rather than emitting an event only.
requirements.acceptance: Stingers heard exactly once, tails respected, thenReturnTo demonstrably executes, interruption/death/retry cancels obsolete returns, overlapping triggers follow explicit priority.

requirements.need: Quantized transitions, explicit interrupt rules, reversible area changes and debounced threat intensity.
requirements.acceptance: Rapid state flips, leaving/reentering areas and unavailable next sections produce no stuck music, clicks, doubled voices or out-of-order reward cues; urgent gameplay SFX remain immediate.

requirements.need: True synchronized bed/pulse/colour/melody layers if the final arrangements benefit; dialogue ducking with separate controls.
requirements.acceptance: Phase-aligned loop sync, bounded polyphony/CPU and gain transitions; no clipping; speech and critical SFX intelligible on phone speaker and mono. Stems remain optional if explicit arrangements sound better.

requirements.need: Deterministic per-section export with sample-accurate loop points, tails, schema/engine provenance and reusable variants.
requirements.acceptance: Same seed/project yields reproducible assets; decoded loop lengths match manifest; no cropped reverb, start clicks or accidental drift; invalid project fails with actionable error.

requirements.need: Bounded music residency across seamless rope and other area transitions; pause/background/resume and save-state coherence.
requirements.acceptance: Target phone and Windows measurements establish storage, memory, decoding and audio-thread budgets; no underruns or duplicate playback after interruptions; no ordinary rope-loading music.
